title: UFW and Azure probe post-change verification
dependencies: both VPN VMs running with Azure VM agent
existing TCP 443 load-balancer probe and rule
operator-reported UFW changes already applied outside this increment

identity_and_permissions.identity: existing GitHub Actions federated Azure identity
required: read Azure network and VM state
invoke one read-only RunShellScript command per VM

network_paths: Azure Load Balancer probe source to 10.20.10.11:443
Azure Load Balancer probe source to 10.20.10.12:443
GitHub-hosted runner to the public load-balancer IPv4 address on TCP 443
security_controls: deterministic analyzer preserves uncertainty and avoids causal overclaim
cost_implications: No new Azure resources. Existing VM, public IP, load-balancer, Azure Monitor and GitHub Actions usage only; incremental cost expected to be negligible but not asserted as zero.
execution_method: Merge-triggered one-shot GitHub Actions workflow after exact-head CI passes.
validation: observe UFW active on both guests
observe at least one TCP 443 allow rule on both guests
observe systemd active and TCP 443 listener on both guests
poll current DipAvailability for both backend IPs
observe VPN-01 success and VPN-02 radius_response failure if the intended scenario is working

failure_and_rollback.failure_behavior: Stop after the single bounded run and upload partial evidence.
failure_and_rollback.rollback: Not applicable because this verification increment performs no mutation.

cleanup: No resources are created. Artifacts expire after 30 days; repository evidence remains durable.
evidence_to_capture: artifact digest and workflow run ID
